content.title: The Chris brown and Usher tour is here! The Usher and Chris brown tour fans have been dreaming of is a reality. Chris brown made it official on his socials today, as did Usher who posted the same teaser trailer for the Raymond and Brown tour leaving fans with one major question what are the Chris brown and ushers tour dates? The Usher Chris brown Tour announcement stole the music news cycle’s headlines on Day 1 of Coachella 2026. If we’re being honest, the Chris brown and Usher tour 2026 might be the biggest concert news of the year. For years, an Usher Chris brown tour was just  fantasy. Now the Chris brown usher tour is happening. While there is no word yet on usher and Chris brown tour dates, we do know usher and Chris brown tour 2026 dates are happening. Usher and Chris brown are two of the biggest r&b icons of the 21st century. Chris brown tour 2026 dates were already highly anticipated, but now that Chris brown and usher have linked up for the r&b tour, it’s no longer a Chris brown tour it’s a usher Chris brown tour and its being called the Raymond and brown tour featuring Chris brown usher and maybe other acts to be announced at a later time. Chris brown Tour dates 2026 was already a hot topic, but an usher and Chris brown concert have been what R&B fans have wanted for years. They now don’t have to dream as Chris brown usher tour 2026 is just months away. Chris brown and Usher have a long history together. Chris Brown’s mom saw Chris brown dancing to Usher’s My Way and knew Chris brown was special. Usher and Chris brown actually met in the 2000s before collaborating on Chris Brown’s New Flame remix in 2014 and again in 2025 on Chris Brown’s It Depends which samples Usher’s Nice & Slow. Usher also appeared at the Breezy Bowl in 2025 in Atlanta. Are you buying tickets for the Chris brown and Usher tour? Let’s talk about it. | Kevan Kenney | Facebook

Millennials will remember Bubba Sparxx and if you do, do you have a favorite Bubbba Sparx song?Kevan Kenney18.4K views · 1d ago1:52In the early 2000s you could pay 50 bucks and beat up most celebrities. It was a bizarre millennial trend that remains a mystery today. Don’t like Snoop Dogg? Ludacris? Joe Budden? Beat them all up in Def Jam Vendetta or Def Jam Fight for NY? Got a problem with Fabolous? Box him in EA Sports Fight Night Round 2. This trend of beating up celebrities goes way deeper. In 1994, Shaquille Oneil, yes SHAQ himself may have started the 90s trend of beating up celebrities in video games when Shaq came out with Shaq Fu a fighting game for the Super Nintendo and Sega Genesis. Then in 1995, there was Rap Jam which was a street basketball game featuring Coolio, Queen Latifah, House of Pain, Flava Flav, Public Enemy, Everlasting, DJ Lethal, Onyx, LL Cool J and more. Remember Wu Tang Shaolin Style for Playstation in 1999? That 90s video game even came with a secret cheat code to unlock the uncensored version of Wu Tang Shaolin Style for Playstation back in 1999. In the 2000s, these games were everywhere. Remember how much people hated Limp Bizkit and Fred Durst in 2001? In games like Fight Club of XBOX and Playstation 2, or WWF Raw or WWF Smackdown Just Bring It you could literally fight and wrestle Fred Durst as a playable character. If you grew up on MTV, you probably remember celebrity death match. Celebrity Deathmatch had a game! You could fight as Busta Rhymes, Anna Nicole Smith, Marilyn Manson, Tommy Lee and tons more. Def Jam Vendetta and Def Jam Fight for NY are definitely still king. You could fight as everybody from Fat Joe to Dmx and back. Did you play any of the 2000s video games or 90s video games? Eminem signed 50 cent in June of 2002 to a joint venture between Shady Records and Aftermath Entertainment. This was at the peak of 50 Cent’s mixtape days and during the zenith of hype around the 50 cent mixtape guess who’s back. Eminem as the story goes flew 50 cent out to Los Angeles a short time after the Marshall Mathers LP dropped. 50 Cent would eventually go on to sign with Eminem, debut with Wanksta, a track off Eminem’s 8 Mile Soundtrack and peaked at No. 13 on the Billboard Hot 100. Millennials will remember the classic MTV music video from 2002 featuring 50 Cent in the Hummer H2. A few months later in January 2003, 50 Cent would drop In Da Club and the rest is history. But how did 50 cent and Eminem meet? It’s all thanks to Cash Money Records and New Orleans legend Juvenile. Juvenile says that Eminem was on of the first major rappers to show him love after back that Azz Up went wild in the summer of 1999. Juvenile lent 50 cent, Tony yayo, Lloyd banks and g unit the mobile recording studio on Juvenile’s tour bus at the time to record their iconic 2000s hip hop G Unit mixtapes. Not only did G unit record on Juvenile’s bus, they met Young Buck on the bus who would eventually join G Unit and be a part of G Unit’s 2003 album Beg For Mercy. Did you know this story?! Fat Joe is a Bronx heavyweight and Hip Hop legend with 90s hits, 2000s throwbacks and 2010s forgotten gems. Fat Joe’s most lucrative moment of Fat Joe’s life came from a Fat Joe track Fat Joe absolutely despised. For Fat Joe, a hardcore street rapper who built his formidable reputation alongside legendary lyricists like Big Pun, the idea of doing a commercial pop crossover with Ashanti felt like a betrayal. Fat Joe Fans who regularly search for the classic big pun fat joe era understand his roots were firmly planted in gritty New York City hip hop of the 1990s and Early 2000s. The dynamic between fat joe big pun was foundational to the Terror Squad. Even today, people look back at the late big pun and marvel at the raw lyricism Fat Joe and Big Pun shared. So, how did Fat Joe end up making a massive mainstream radio anthem with Irv Gotti, Ja Rule and Ashanti? The story begins in 2002, during the absolute peak of the Murda Inc reign. Think Mesmerize, Livin It Up, Foolish, Put it on Me etc. At three in the morning, Irv Gotti called Fat Joe and played a beat over the phone that flipped a legendary Tina Turner sample. Irv Gotti and Ja Rule envisioned a massive collaboration for Fat Joe and Jennifer Lopez. When Fat Joe heard the reference track, Fat Joe fell in love with the vocals of the unknown demo singer named Ashanti. Fat Joe gambled on the unknown rookie Ashanti over JLo, a decision that drastically impacted the overall fat joe net worth for decades to come. What’s Luv? Was Released to massive fanfare, Fat Joe - What’s Luv peaked at number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and remains a streaming juggernaut today. It is widely considered the ultimate fat joe song by mainstream Fat Joe audiences, even though Fat Joe notoriously hated it because Fat Joe felt it was a blatant pop clone that compromised Fat Joe’s street credibility. Fat Joe openly admits Fat Joe still cannot stand What’s Love. If you look at Fat Joe’s entire catalog, including the massive club anthem lean back fat joe created with Remy Ma and terror squad, nothing touches the commercial success of this Ashanti collaboration on What’s Luv with Fat Joe.Kevan Kenney8K views · April 7 at 1:10 AM1:58Tupac Shakur had among the most legendary trajectories in the entire history of music, not only 90’s Hip Hop. 2pac executed the single greatest five-year run the hip hop industry has ever witnessed from 1991 through 1996. From Tupac’s explosive mainstream debut in 1991 until the tragic passing of Tupac Shakur in 1996, the sheer volume and cultural impact of 2pac’s output remain entirely unmatched. To truly understand Tupac’s monumental hip hop legacy, you have to look beyond just the standard tupac song that plays on hip hop radio to this day; you must examine 2pac’s relentless, almost superhuman work ethic. In a window of merely half a decade, Tupac shaker seamlessly transitioned into Hollywood, commanding the screen in seven different feature films and delivering unforgettable performances in cinematic street classics like Poetic Justice, Juice, and Above the Rim. But 2pac’s true devotion always remained anchored in the recording studio. Insiders from that era notoriously reported that 2 pac possessed a frantic urgency, recording vocals at a pace that baffled his 90’s rap peers. Tupac laid down over 500 unreleased tupac songs during this intense period, leaving behind enough material for seven posthumous 2pac albums. Tupac’s influence was so massive that Tupac Shakur’s introspective masterpiece, Me Against The World, debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard charts while he was actively serving a prison sentence. Cultural fascination with Tupac’s life never wanes. Decades later, 2pac remains a legend. The collaborations involving snoop dogg tupac history continue to spark discussions among hip hop purists and inspired the 2 of Amerikaz Most Wanted wine in 2026. Whether 90’s hip hop fans are revisiting 2pac’s classic tupac catalog, exploring the details surrounding the tupac death investigation, or analyzing the chemistry whenever 2pac and snoop dogg linked up, Tupac shakur’s mythos only grows.
